result:
I found 3 of the 6 FEBio pilot runs at a third to half of normal CPU speed and re-pinned their cores. All 6 now run at 346–350 % CPU.

**Inventory (05:31)**
- **CPU:** 14.3 of the 32-core quota in use before the fix, 20.9 after. No throttling (0 of 51 periods). Load average 25.8.
- **Memory:** 137.0 / 137.4 GB, but only 19.1 GB is process memory; the other 116 GB is file cache the system can free. No out-of-memory kills. /raid has 2.6 TB free.
- **GPUs:** mine are GPU 1 (3 runs), GPU 3 (1) and GPU 4 (2). GPU 0 is full with another user's work. GPUs 2, 5 and 6 are idle for me; 6 is completely free.
- **FEBio queue:** 6 running (pilotCR2 p061/p083/p120/p129, pilotR9_p061, pilotST_p061 w_flexion), 0 waiting, 2522 done, 2 failed. 4 runs finished in the last 3 h, none in the last hour.
- **Task queue:** 0 waiting, 0 running. The 1 done and 5 failed are old gate2 tasks from 10-28.

**Health:** all 6 logs are still being written (latest line ≤ 13 s old), and every tmux service from `resume_all.sh` is up. Nothing is hung, dead or crash-looping.

**What I changed:** the 3 slow runs had core sets spread across different memory regions (NUMA nodes). The kernel's automatic NUMA balancing kept all 4 threads of each run on the 1–2 cores next to its memory. I moved each run (and its parent `h31` process) to 4 idle cores in that one region:

| Run | Cores before → after | CPU before → after |
|---|---|---|
| pilotR9_p061 | 9,29,31,32 → 32–35 | 109 % → 347 % (all 4 threads were on core 32) |
| pilotST_p061 w_flexion | 6,7,23,24 → 23–26 | 178 % → 347 % |
| pilotCR2_p120 | 5,15–17 → 16–19 | 182 % → 347 % |

The move also ended a shared core 9 between pilotR9_p061 and pilotCR2_p083. I did not restart the scheduler: pilotST_p061 is a CPU split run, which the old scheduler wrongly marks as ended after a restart.

Higher CPU use doesn't yet show the runs actually go faster. I saved each run's current time step in `status.json`, so the next hourly check can compare the rate. Before the fix, pilotR9_p061 was at t = 3.313 of 3.5, gaining 0.024 per hour.

**Needs a person:**
- The code that assigns cores to new runs (`h06`/`h18`, outside what I may edit) should pick each run's cores from one NUMA node (cores 0–15, 16–31, …). Otherwise this slowdown comes back with every new run.
- Both queues are empty apart from these 6 pilots; about 11 quota cores and GPUs 2/5/6 are idle. Queue the next batch if one is planned.
- Only 1 of 10 pilot runs since 23:29 ended normally (reported last hour) — still open.

I also saved a note to my memory on how to spot and fix this slowdown.

Files are in `work/agents/foreman/`:
- report_20261104_0531.md
- status.json

The 3 actions are also logged in `work/ops/foreman_actions.log`.
